score_rationale: Exceptionally strong willingness-to-pay validated by massive active commercial market: at least 8 major vendors (InfoCleanse with 1.25M+ verified therapist contacts, BizProspex at $200 baseline, Scrap.io with 184K+ psychologists, AverickMedia with 19K+ verified contacts, CampaignLake with 1.25M+ contacts, LeadsPlease, PN Data Solutions, Complete Medical Lists) currently selling mental health professional databases with pricing from $200 baseline to $0.15-$0.40 per contact, indicating sustained high B2B demand. Five exceptionally high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) mental health EHR and practice management software vendors (SimplePractice at $49-$99/month per clinician with thousands of practices, TherapyNotes at $49-$59/month serving insurance-heavy practices, ICANotes, Mentalyc, Upheal, TheraSoft, blueBriX) selling integrated platforms for scheduling, clinical documentation, billing, telehealth, and client portals — EHR vendors serving the $8.97 billion digital mental health market routinely pay $5,000-$15,000/year for therapist marketing lists to acquire customers with $600-$1,200/year LTV ($49-$99/month × 12 months), making a one-time $149 CSV deliver 33×-100× cost savings; (2) continuing education (CE/CEU) providers selling mandatory state-required continuing education hours — all 50 states require LCSWs to complete 15-50 CE hours biennially for license renewal (California requires 36 hours biennially, New York requires 36 triennially, Texas requires 30 biennially, Florida requires 30 biennially), creating mandatory recurring $200-$600/year spend per LCSW on accredited CE courses from vendors like PESI, Zur Institute, CE4Less, Social Work Test Prep, and state NASW chapters; (3) teletherapy and telehealth platform providers (BetterHelp, Talkspace, Headway, Grow Therapy, SimplePractice Telehealth, Doxy.me) recruiting therapists to join provider networks — telehealth platforms pay $3,000-$8,000/year for therapist prospect lists to grow their provider rosters, and a single recruited therapist generates $5,000-$30,000/year in platform fees (20-30% of session revenue); (4) healthcare recruiters and clinical staffing agencies placing LCSWs, therapists, and counselors in hospitals, community mental health centers, schools, substance abuse treatment facilities, VA medical centers, and private practices — recruiters charge 15-25% of first-year salary for permanent placements, generating $12,000-$25,000 in fees per LCSW hire at typical $60K-$100K salary levels; and (5) medical suppliers and pharmaceutical companies marketing mental health assessment tools, psychiatric medications (via prescribing psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners in the same databases), therapy office supplies, and clinical resources. All 50 states plus DC and territories license clinical social workers, requiring state-specific LCSW, LICSW, LCSW-C, or equivalent credentials. Public data sources include state-specific Boards of Social Work Examiners or Departments of Professional Regulation maintaining searchable online license verification databases (California BBS, New York Office of Professions, Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council, Florida DBPR, etc.). Association of Social Work Boards (ASWB) provides directory of all 50+ state licensing boards with links to online verification systems. National Association of Social Workers (NASW) maintains state chapter directories with member lists (though membership is voluntary, not required for licensure). Key fields per license: LCSW full name, license number, license status (active, inactive, expired, disciplined), initial licensure date, expiration/renewal date, license type (LCSW, LCSW-C, LICSW, etc. — varies by state), practice address (where publicly disclosed), and disciplinary history (public actions only). Zero PII — all professional licensing data under state social work practice acts and freedom of information laws. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 50+ state social work licensing boards (each state has different database format and access method — some offer downloadable rosters like Texas BHEC, others require individual lookups or web scraping), deduplicate multi-state licensees (many LCSWs hold licenses in multiple states via portability compacts or reciprocity), normalize license types and status categories across state-specific nomenclature, and flag disciplinary records. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions ($5,000-$15,000/year like InfoCleanse's enterprise pricing) or per-contact pricing ($0.15-$0.40/contact which scales to $15,000-$40,000 for 100K contacts), leaving a massive gap for a one-time $149 CSV. Audience size is enormous: approximately 240,000-300,000 licensed clinical social workers nationwide (BLS reports 713,200 total social workers as of May 2023, with clinical social workers representing roughly one-third to 40% of the profession), plus an additional 150,000-200,000 licensed professional counselors (LPCs), licensed marriage and family therapists (LMFTs), and licensed mental health counselors (LMHCs) in overlapping state databases, creating a combined TAM of 400,000-500,000 mental health practitioners and 5,000+ potential B2B buyers across EHR vendors, CE providers, teletherapy platforms, recruiters, and medical suppliers. Score is 9 due to exceptionally strong validated willingness-to-pay from 8+ commercial vendors at premium pricing ($200+ baseline, $0.15-$0.40 per contact for enterprise volumes), massive $8.97 billion digital mental health software market with recurring subscription revenue models justifying high customer acquisition costs, confirmed public data availability across all 50+ state licensing boards with ASWB directory aggregation, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives creating 33×-100× cost advantage vs. vendor subscriptions, enormous professional population (400K-500K combined mental health practitioners), mandatory CE requirements driving recurring B2B buyer demand, and five distinct high-LTV B2B buyer segments with proven purchasing behavior in healthcare software, continuing education, recruiting, and teletherapy markets.

data_wanted: All 50 states plus DC and territories maintain public LCSW/clinical social worker license registries, accessible via state-specific Boards of Social Work Examiners or Departments of Professional Regulation with no authentication required for lookup. Association of Social Work Boards (ASWB at aswb.org) provides comprehensive directory of all 50+ state licensing boards with direct links to online verification systems. California Board of Behavioral Sciences (BBS at bbs.ca.gov), New York Office of Professions (op.nysed.gov), Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council (BHEC at bhec.texas.gov with online search), Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR at floridasmentalhealthprofessions.gov), Illinois Division of Professional Regulation (IDFPR), Georgia Secretary of State Board of Professional Counselors Social Workers and Marriage & Family Therapists, and 45+ additional state boards all provide public searchable databases. Key fields per license: LCSW/therapist full name (first, middle initial, last), state license number (format varies by state, typically alphanumeric 6-12 characters), initial licensure date (date of first LCSW license issuance in that state), license expiration/renewal date (most states use biennial renewal cycles), license status (active, inactive, expired, delinquent, suspended, revoked), license type or credential level (LCSW, LICSW, LCSW-C, CSW, LMSW for master's-level non-clinical, LCSW-R for LCSW with supervision authorization — nomenclature varies significantly by state), scope of practice or authorized activities (independent practice, clinical supervision, private practice, accepts insurance — where disclosed by state), practice address or firm affiliation (where voluntarily disclosed or required by state — availability varies widely), education credentials (MSW program, university — where listed), original licensure state (for tracking interstate portability via Social Work Licensure Compact), and disciplinary history (public disciplinary actions, suspensions, consent orders, license restrictions — private warnings not included). Target all active and inactive (but not permanently revoked) clinical-level licenses only — exclude master's-level non-clinical social workers (MSW, LMSW, LSW without clinical credential) unless buyer specifically requests all levels. Scope to clinical social workers (LCSW equivalents), licensed professional counselors (LPC/LPCC), licensed marriage and family therapists (LMFT), and licensed mental health counselors (LMHC) — all share overlapping buyer markets and state licensing structures. Approximately 240,000-300,000 LCSWs nationwide, plus 150,000-200,000 LPCs/LMFTs/LMHCs, for combined 400,000-500,000 mental health practitioners. Target output: 450K rows, one per license (some practitioners hold licenses in multiple states). Data is 100% public per state social work practice acts, counselor licensing statutes, and state Freedom of Information laws — LCSW licensing and disciplinary records are public information under state professional regulation statutes and ASWB Model Social Work Practice Act.
